signal.title: OdorSpaces: Visual-Olfactory Embodied Navigation in 3D Environments
signal.summary: 这项研究聚焦机器人在动态或开放环境中的运动规划，尝试让路径不仅能到达目标，也能满足安全和物理约束。

editorial.intro: 这项研究聚焦机器人在动态或开放环境中的运动规划，尝试让路径不仅能到达目标，也能满足安全和物理约束。
editorial.why_it_matters: 运动规划连接感知、世界模型和执行控制，是具身智能从算法演示走向可靠运行的关键环节。
editorial.watch_next: 继续核对复杂场景、碰撞率和真实机器人上的执行效果。

evidence.title: OdorSpaces: Visual-Olfactory Embodied Navigation in 3D Environments
evidence.excerpt: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. We introduce OdorSpaces, a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation. OdorSpaces augments Habitat-Sim with 3D odor transport and dispersion simulated by Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS), enabling agents to navigate photorealistic indoor environments using both visual and olfactory observations. The benchmark includes two representative source-seeking scenarios: invisible gas-leak localization and early-stage fire localization. We develop an initial multimodal reinforcement learning policy that integrates visual observations and olfactory measurements over time. Experiments show that the policy outperforms a diverse set of baselines, establishing a strong reference for future research on visual-olfactory embodied navigation.
